content.text:
Short answer
- For adult office workers in California, CDC and California (CDPH) public‑health guidance are aligned: stay home while acutely ill with influenza and do not return until at least 24 hours after your fever has resolved without the use of fever‑reducing medicines; resume normal work once symptoms have improved and you meet that fever‑free criterion while continuing routine respiratory hygiene. ([archive.cdc.gov](https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/h1n1flu/business/guidance/?utm_source=openai))

Key points (with sources)
- CDC (general / business guidance): persons with influenza‑like illness should remain home and may return to work only after they have been fever‑free (temperature <100°F/37.8°C) for at least 24 hours without fever‑reducing medicines; businesses should encourage non‑punitive sick leave and promote hand/respiratory hygiene. ([archive.cdc.gov](https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/h1n1flu/business/guidance/?utm_source=openai))  
- CDPH (California): mirrors that approach for community settings—individuals “may return to work/school/childcare after symptoms have resolved including at least 24 hours have passed since resolution of fever without the use of fever‑reducing medications”—and emphasizes encouraging sick leave and consulting local health departments as needed. ([cdph.ca.gov](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/OPA/Pages/CAHAN/Early-Respiratory-Syncytial-Virus-and-Seasonal-Influenza-Activity.aspx?utm_source=openai)
